name: Blue Marine Foundation
scale_note: Helped establish large marine protected areas including Ascension Island's 445,000 sq km reserve

name: Coral Triangle Initiative on Coral Reefs, Fisheries and Food Security (CTI-CFF)
scale_note: Multilateral partnership of six countries: Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Solomon Islands and Timor-Leste

name: CORDIO East Africa
scale_note: Research and conservation organization monitoring coral reefs and supporting community-managed areas in the Western Indian Ocean

name: Deep Sea Conservation Coalition (DSCC)
scale_note: Global coalition of more than 130 organizations campaigning against bottom trawling and deep-sea mining

name: Deep-Ocean Stewardship Initiative (DOSI)
scale_note: Global network integrating deep-ocean science into policy through working groups on deep-sea minerals, biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction and more

name: Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network (GCRMN)
scale_note: Operational network of the International Coral Reef Initiative with 10 regional nodes; produces the Status of Coral Reefs of the World report

name: Global Fishing Watch
scale_note: Uses satellite data and vessel tracking to support ocean governance and marine protected area enforcement

name: High Seas Alliance
scale_note: Coalition of 70+ NGOs plus IUCN advancing the High Seas Treaty (BBNJ) and high-seas marine protected areas

name: IFREMER (French Research Institute for Exploitation of the Sea)
scale_note: France's only public institute entirely dedicated to marine science; operates a national oceanographic research fleet

name: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC)
Marine Biodiversity Observation Network (MBON)
scale_note: Thematic node of GEO BON with regional networks across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Arctic

name: Marine Conservation Institute
scale_note: Runs the Blue Parks award and the Marine Protection Atlas global MPA database

name: MigraMar
scale_note: Scientific network whose research helped expand Eastern Pacific MPA coverage from 156,000 sq km (2010) to 630,000 sq km (2022) through the Swimways Initiative

name: National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research (NIWA)
Nekton
scale_note: Ocean exploration nonprofit running deep-sea expeditions and co-leading the Ocean Census marine species discovery program

name: NOAA Ocean Exploration
scale_note: US federal ocean exploration program operating NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer; mapped 339,864 square kilometers of seafloor in 2025

name: NOAA PMEL Acoustics Program
scale_note: Operates the Ocean Noise Reference Station Network of hydrophone moorings characterizing ocean soundscapes and monitoring whales

name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS)
scale_note: IOC-UNESCO global platform with about 200 million species observation records covering roughly 205,000 marine species from 99 countries

name: Ocean Exploration Trust
scale_note: Operates E/V Nautilus; since 2009 completed 180 expeditions and mapped over 1.3 million square kilometers of seafloor

name: Ocean Networks Canada
scale_note: Operates cabled ocean observatories with hydrophones for passive acoustic monitoring across the Pacific, Arctic, Atlantic and Southern oceans

name: OceanCare
scale_note: Marine conservation organization with UN Special Consultative Status; programs on underwater noise and deep-sea mining

name: Schmidt Ocean Institute
scale_note: Nonprofit operating research vessel Falkor (too); had mapped roughly 1 million square kilometers of seafloor by 2019

name: Western Indian Ocean Marine Science Association (WIOMSA)
scale_note: Regional marine science membership organization spanning 10 Western Indian Ocean countries

name: Whale Sound (BC Hydrophone Network)
scale_note: Community network operating 22 hydrophone stations along the British Columbia coast to monitor whales and ocean noise

name: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI)
scale_note: Operates the human-occupied submersible Alvin and ROV Jason/Medea

name: Charles Darwin Foundation
scale_note: In 2023 its deep-ocean program logged 120 field dive days using ROVs and submersibles, including the discovery of previously undocumented deep-sea coral reefs in the Galapagos Marine Reserve.

name: Marine Protected Areas South Africa
scale_note: As of its 2019 network expansion, South Africa's 24 mainland MPAs covered about 0.43% of national ocean area, with 0.16% under no-take protection, and the country recognizes 18 CBD-listed EBSAs.

name: ASEAN Centre for Biodiversity
scale_note: Its ASEAN ENMAPS project works to strengthen management of marine protected area networks across large marine ecosystems in a region that holds roughly a third of the world's coastal and marine habitats.

name: Minderoo-UWA Deep-Sea Research Centre
scale_note: Supported by a five-year grant from the Minderoo Foundation's Flourishing Oceans initiative, it specializes in abyssal (3,000-6,000m) and hadal (6,000-11,000m) depths.
